about: GH #326 phase 5 parity cases. The IDE buffer is authoritative whenever it is readable. The Rust derivation and frozen Kotlin floor both defer a pending local delivery, converge exact equality, and otherwise publish the IDE buffer into the controller projection. Controller containment, shadow, disk, restart, and retained-state facts are diagnostics only. The one exception is the controller's op record of its own binary-authored writes (#acceptedwriterollforward): when it names the buffer, or the settled shadow with a clean merge from it, as a generation those writes alone carried to canonical, the accepted writes roll forward onto the buffer; the frozen floor predates that rule and still adopts.
